name: Scout Mendez
life: “I still remember the little whale painted on my child's rain barrel.” Thursday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Scout can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: My child thinks there's a whale in the harbor. The skipper invited us to listen through the deck.
appearance: Scout has a smooth side part with one rebellious curl, a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, and a favorite piece of clothing, a moss-green cardigan. It usually goes with a watch on a cracked leather band. When somebody else has the floor, Scout gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Scout gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Scout privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To let the child hear the hum through the deck.
family: Hector Lang is Scout’s stepsibling. Scout chooses whether to use it. Hector saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The hospital radio*, Hector says, “I used to tune the coast forecast for my father.”
connections: Anita Gill. A child with a whale story gives the wedding recording a new pair of listeners.

reactions.response: Scout writes down the shift time accurately, then helps them explain the circumstances without having to tell the whole room.
